# fjordrun_function_environment (Resource)

A function's settings in an additional environment, like `fjordrun_service_environment` for services. Nothing is created: functions exist in every environment of their project. Use it for every environment except the one `fjordrun_function` manages. Code is shared by all environments and belongs to `fjordrun_function`. The API can't reset an instance to defaults, so destroying this resource leaves the settings as they are.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "team_id" {
  type = string
}

resource "fjordrun_project" "shop" {
  team_id = var.team_id
  name    = "shop"
}

resource "fjordrun_environment" "staging" {
  project_id = fjordrun_project.shop.id
  name       = "staging"
}

resource "fjordrun_function" "hello" {
  project_id     = fjordrun_project.shop.id
  environment_id = fjordrun_project.shop.default_environment_id
  name           = "hello"
  files          = { "index.mjs" = "export default () => Response.json({ hello: 'world' });" }
  depends_on     = [fjordrun_environment.staging]
}

resource "fjordrun_function_environment" "hello_staging" {
  function_id    = fjordrun_function.hello.id
  environment_id = fjordrun_environment.staging.id
  memory_mb      = 128
  auto_deploy    = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `environment_id` (String) Environment ID.
- `function_id` (String) Function ID.

### Optional

- `auth` (String) `public` (default): anyone with the URL. `token`: requests need `token` in the `token_header` header.
- `auto_deploy` (Boolean) Deploy when this resource is created or changes. Leave out to use the provider's `auto_deploy` (default `true`). With `false` the change is saved and goes live with the next deployment, which `fjordrun_deployment` makes explicit.
- `concurrency` (Number) Requests in flight per instance before another starts (1-100, default 10).
- `entry` (String) The file that exports the handler, relative to the code root. Defaults to `index.mjs` or `main.py`.
- `idle_timeout_s` (Number) How long an instance stays up after its last request, billed as instance time (30-900, default 120). The Trial plan fixes it at 60: any other value is an error there.
- `max_replicas` (Number) Most instances (1-50, default 1). Plans limit it.
- `memory_mb` (Number) Memory: 128, 256 (default), 512, 1024, 2048 or 4096 MB. Plans limit it. CPU follows from memory.
- `on_destroy` (String) What destroying this resource does to the function in this environment: `stop` (default) removes its active deployment; `keep` leaves it running.
- `rotate_token_trigger` (String) Change this value to rotate `token`. With `auth = "token"`, rotating redeploys a running function, whatever `auto_deploy` says: the old token keeps working until the new deployment is live.
- `runtime` (String) `node22` (default) or `python312`. Changing it moves a default `entry` along.
- `timeout_s` (Number) Seconds a request may run (1-900, default 30). Plans limit it.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `wait` (Boolean) With `auto_deploy`: wait until the deployment finishes, up to the `create`/`update` timeout (default 30 minutes), and fail the apply unless it succeeds.

### Read-Only

- `code_sha256` (String) Hash of the saved inline code, shared by all environments. Null for code from GitHub.
- `deployed_sha256` (String) Hash of the inline code the live deployment runs. Equal to `code_sha256` once the saved code is deployed.
- `id` (String) `function_id/environment_id`.
- `status` (String) Status in this environment: `inactive`, `building`, `deploying`, `active`, `sleeping`, `failed`...
- `token` (String, Sensitive) The token callers send, with `auth = "token"`. Null otherwise. Each environment has its own.
- `token_header` (String) The header that carries the token, with `auth = "token"`.
- `url` (String) The function's URL in this environment.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# function_id/environment_id
terraform import fjordrun_function_environment.hello_staging cccccccc-cccc-cccc-cccc-cccccccccccc/88888888-8888-8888-8888-888888888888
```
